candidate_relations.reason: Langerhans cell histiocytosis matches the reference diagnosis exactly; the clinical and imaging features (destructive bony lesion of maxillary sinus anterior wall, soft-tissue mass with fluid-fluid level on MRI, rapid enlargement, young child, periorbital swelling) are classic for LCH.
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis is a vasculitic/granulomatous condition; while it can involve sinuses and orbits, it is a distinct entity from LCH and is uncommon in toddlers.
Orbital cellulitis was the initial clinical diagnosis but was excluded by imaging showing a destructive bony lesion; it is a differential/manifestation rather than the final diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Clinical presentation mimicked cellulitis but imaging reveals destructive mass

candidate_relations.reason: Orbital neuroblastoma (metastatic) typically presents with bilateral periorbital ecchymosis and is a metastatic deposit; the lesion here is centered on the maxillary sinus anterior wall without features pointing to neuroblastoma.
Ewing sarcoma is a primary bone malignancy; while it can cause destructive lesions, it is a distinct entity from LCH and less characteristic in this age group and location.
Granulocytic sarcoma (myeloid sarcoma) is associated with leukemia/myeloid malignancy; no hematologic abnormalities are noted in this case, making it a different entity from LCH.
Lymphoma is a distinct hematopoietic malignancy; while it can present as an orbital mass, it is a different entity from LCH.
Esthesioneuroblastoma arises from olfactory epithelium in the nasal vault and is extremely rare in toddlers; this is a distinct entity from LCH.

Rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common primary orbital malignancy in children and is a key differential, but it is a distinct entity from LCH; the destructive anterior maxillary sinus wall lesion with fluid-fluid level is more characteristic of LCH.
Orbital lymphangioma is a vascular malformation; while it can show fluid-fluid levels, it does not cause bony destruction of the maxillary sinus wall and is a distinct entity.
Orbital granuloma is a nonspecific descriptive term for a granulomatous process; it does not equate to LCH as a specific diagnosis.
Invasive aspergillosis typically occurs in immunocompromised patients; this child is immunocompetent with no relevant history, making this a different and unlikely entity.
Ewing sarcoma (alternate spelling of C005) is a distinct primary bone malignancy, not equivalent to LCH.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different diagnostic entity (duplicate of C005 with variant spelling)

case_quality_flags: C005 and C013 appear to be duplicates (Ewing's sarcoma vs Ewing sarcoma); both evaluated independently as not_equivalent
